title: What does LoanBrokerCoverClawback do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of LoanBrokerCoverClawback and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, LoanBrokerCoverClawback lets a qualifying issuer recover issued first-loss capital from a loan broker's cover. [1]

The operation belongs to the documented LendingProtocol and interacts with the token's issuer permissions. First-loss cover is a risk buffer, not a guarantee that all loans will be repaid. Check the broker, issuance and clawback eligibility. A legal claim against a borrower is distinct from the ledger authority to change this cover balance. [1]

The LoanBrokerCoverClawback reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using LoanBrokerCoverClawback, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
